blocks.text: In A2-22 You wrote the first brief formal emails. Now write complete letters: with place and date, recipient, object, opening formula, a body organized in paragraphs, closure and attachments. Learn the formulas for the most common types of letter (information request, registration, complaint, apology, thanksgiving, candidacy), the forms of courtesy of the standard Arabic ( ⁧أَرْجُو التَّكَرُّمَ بِـ⁩ …, ⁧يُسْعِدُنِي أَنْ⁩ …, ⁧وَتَفَضَّلُوا بِقَبُولِ⁩ ...) and the difference between formal letter, semi-formal email and informal message. On examination B1 The formal letter is one of the two writing tests. Two weeks.

Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. set up a complete Arab formal letter, with all its parts;
2. choose opening and closing formulas suitable for the recipient;
3. write letters of request, complaint, apology, thanks and candidacy;
4. from an informal register to a formal register ( ⁧أُرِيدُ⁩ → ⁧أَوَدُّ أَنْ⁩ …; ⁧أَرْسِلُوا⁩ → ⁧أَرْجُو التَّكَرُّمَ بِإِرْسَالِ⁩ …);
5. write a formal letter of 120–150 words, clear, courteous and without dialect.

1. The plural of respect. To a formal recipient we address the plural: ⁧إِلَيْكُمْ⁩ , ⁧رَدُّكُمْ⁩ , ⁧تَفَضَّلُوا⁩ , even if it is a lonely. You write to the singular ( ⁧أَنَا⁩ ), unless he writes on behalf of an office ( ⁧نَحْنُ⁩ ).

3. The nominal style. The maṣdar make the text more formal and shorter: ⁧أَرْجُو إِرْسَالَ⁩ ... instead of ⁧أَرْجُو أَنْ تُرْسِلُوا⁩ ….

Read a letter aloud (for example, dictate it to someone or read it over the phone): formulas are read with desinences, because they are fixed: taḥiyyatan ṭayyibatan wa-baʿdu · wa-tafaḍḍalū bi-qabūli fāʾiqi l-iḥtirām. Exercise to breathe, with a break only before ⁧وَبَعْدُ⁩ .
